title: Insurer Program Agreements — Assignment Response Terms Card
content:
Three terms of the Insurer Program Agreements govern how the network responds to a claim assignment from the insurer and whether the assignment can still be withdrawn later:

- **Response window** — the hours within which the network accepts or declines an assignment (a whole number of hours).
- **Decline permitted** — whether the network may decline an assignment in its service area.
- **Withdrawal after repair order** — whether an assignment may still be withdrawn once a repair order has been opened for it.

| Agreement tier | Response window (hours) | Decline permitted | Withdrawal after repair order opened |
|---|---|---|---|
| Network Referral Agreement | 24 | Yes | No |
| Select Direct Repair Agreement | 4 | Yes | No |
| Preferred Direct Repair Agreement | 4 | Yes | No |
| Premier Direct Repair Agreement | 2 | No | No |
| Managed Repair Program Agreement | 2 | No | No |
| Enterprise Master Services Agreement | 1 | No | No |

## On the card

- The response window shortens as the tier rises, from 24 hours under a Network Referral Agreement to 1 hour under an Enterprise Master Services Agreement.
- Declining an assignment in the service area is permitted under the Network Referral, Select and Preferred tiers, and not permitted under the Premier, Managed and Enterprise tiers.
- No tier permits withdrawing an assignment once a repair order has been opened for it.

## Illustration (hypothetical time)

An assignment received at 10:00 under a Preferred Direct Repair Agreement is accepted or declined within 4 hours, that is by 14:00. The same assignment under an Enterprise Master Services Agreement has a response window of 1 hour, ending at 11:00; as that tier does not permit declining an assignment in the service area, an assignment in the service area is accepted within that hour. The clock times are invented for the illustration.
